epics.title: [Now] Auth, Users, and Access Hardening
epics.summary: Stabilize authentication, protected access, profile management, and owner-managed user administration for production use.
dependencies: Platform mail behavior must remain compatible with password reset
Shared role and auth contracts must remain aligned between backend and frontend
exitCriteria: Login, refresh, logout, and password reset flows are deterministic
Owner-only user administration rules are explicit and regression-tested
Frontend route protection matches backend authorization truth

subIssues.title: [Auth][Now] Close remaining token lifecycle and session-state gaps
deliverables: Audit login, refresh, logout, forgot-password, and reset-password flows end to end
Confirm token expiry, invalidation, and stale-session handling across API and UI
Document the expected success and failure responses for each auth transition
acceptance: Auth state transitions are consistent across backend and frontend
Expired or invalid credentials fail explicitly without stale UI state
No duplicate auth business rules exist in the frontend

subIssues.title: [Users][Now] Validate owner-managed user lifecycle and profile editing
deliverables: Review user creation, activation, deactivation, and role updates
Verify owner self-protection and cashier boundary rules
Check profile editing flows for validation and synchronization gaps
acceptance: Only owners can manage store staff
Role and activation changes persist correctly
Profile screens reflect saved state and backend errors clearly

subIssues.title: [Auth+Users][Now] Add release checklist for access-control regressions
deliverables: Define the critical manual test scenarios for owner and cashier accounts
Cover protected route redirects, disabled accounts, and reset-password flows
Document the data and environment prerequisites for verification
acceptance: A maintainer can validate access-control behavior without source-code guesswork
Owner and cashier regressions are easy to detect before release
Critical auth flows have explicit expected outcomes

epics.title: [Now] Catalog, Inventory, and Alerts Integrity
epics.summary: Stabilize category and product lifecycle rules, inventory integrity, and alert derivation before operational rollout.
dependencies: Catalog rules must stay aligned with shared product and category contracts
Alerts depend on accurate inventory and expiry state
exitCriteria: Catalog updates do not create inconsistent inventory behavior
Low-stock and expiry alerts reflect real stock state
Operators can trust inventory visibility and warning surfaces

subIssues.title: [Catalog][Now] Standardize category and product lifecycle rules
deliverables: Review category activation constraints and product-category linkage
Confirm product validation for pricing, SKU/barcode identity, and stock thresholds
Trace shared catalog DTOs into all consuming screens
acceptance: Catalog constraints are enforced by the backend consistently
Frontend forms mirror backend validation without duplicating rules
Shared catalog contracts remain the source of truth

subIssues.title: [Inventory][Now] Lock down stock movement integrity and operator workflows
deliverables: Audit stock movement updates, zero-stock handling, and threshold evaluation
Review inventory lists, filters, search, and adjustment entry points
Validate edge cases around missing expiry dates and inactive catalog items
acceptance: Inventory mutations preserve consistent stock state
Critical stock states are visible to operators without ambiguity
Edge cases are handled predictably across API and UI

subIssues.title: [Alerts][Now] Verify in-app alert generation and escalation behavior
deliverables: Trace low-stock and expiry alert derivation from inventory conditions
Check unread counts, mark-read flows, and workspace/dropdown synchronization
Document how optional email escalation behaves when mail infrastructure is unavailable
acceptance: Alert generation matches inventory truth
Unread state remains synchronized across alert entry points
Email escalation boundaries are explicit and operationally safe

epics.title: [Now] Sales, Dashboard, and Reporting Reliability
epics.summary: Stabilize checkout, sales history, dashboard KPIs, and reporting semantics so operators can trust store data end to end.
dependencies: Sales depends on stable catalog and inventory behavior
Dashboard and reports depend on consistent sales aggregates and timezone semantics
exitCriteria: Checkout totals and inventory side effects remain consistent
Dashboard and reports use documented backend metric definitions
Receipt and history flows stay aligned with sales contracts

subIssues.title: [Sales][Now] Audit checkout totals, receipts, and sales history behavior
deliverables: Review cart submission, sale item persistence, payment-mode handling, and receipt payloads
Validate POS interaction speed, receipt navigation, and sales history filtering
Eliminate any duplicated total or line-item assumptions outside backend logic
acceptance: Checkout persists correct totals and line items
Receipts and sales history reflect the same source data
Frontend sales flows do not drift from backend truth

subIssues.title: [Reports][Now] Align dashboard KPIs, reports, and timezone windows
deliverables: Map each dashboard metric and report widget to an explicit backend definition
Review date-range and timezone semantics for daily and period-based reports
Check chart, table, and export consistency against the same dataset
acceptance: Metrics mean the same thing across dashboard and reports
Timezone-sensitive windows behave consistently
Displayed and exported report data stays aligned

subIssues.title: [Sales+Reports][Now] Create operations QA pack for cashier and owner flows
deliverables: Define critical cashier checkout and owner reporting scenarios
Cover error states, empty states, and cross-module data dependency checks
List the exact expected outcomes for manual release verification
acceptance: Store operations can be verified quickly before a release
Cashier and owner workflows have explicit regression coverage
Known dependencies are documented for reproducible testing

epics.title: [Now] Platform, Mail, Health, and Release Readiness
epics.summary: Keep shared contracts, Prisma, Docker, health checks, and mail delivery aligned so deployment behavior is predictable.
dependencies: Every module depends on shared contracts and coherent schema behavior
Auth reset and alert escalation depend on stable mail behavior
exitCriteria: Core build, test, and compose flows are reproducible
Health and readiness semantics match actual runtime state
Schema, seed, and shared contract drift are visible and controlled

subIssues.title: [Platform][Now] Reconcile shared contracts, Prisma schema, and seed data
deliverables: Audit shared-types and shared-utils usage across backend and frontend
Review Prisma schema and migrations against real business flows
Confirm seed data still supports meaningful operator validation
acceptance: Contract duplication is removed or documented explicitly
Schema behavior matches current product logic
Seed data remains useful for end-to-end verification

subIssues.title: [Health+Mail][Now] Tighten readiness checks and operational notification behavior
deliverables: Review health endpoint semantics for database, mail, and runtime readiness
Trace Docker health checks and startup ordering against real app readiness
Document mail verification and failure behavior for local and hosted environments
acceptance: Health signals have clear operational meaning
Container readiness does not overstate application readiness
Mail behavior under valid and invalid configuration is explicit

subIssues.title: [Release][Now] Define minimum deployment and rollback checklist
deliverables: List the commands and checks required before release
Capture rollback assumptions for schema, seed, and app deployment changes
Document the post-deploy smoke tests for owner and cashier workflows
acceptance: Release verification is concise and repeatable
Rollback assumptions are known before deployment
Core production smoke tests are documented clearly

epics.title: [Next] Supplier and Procurement Foundations
epics.summary: Extend the platform beyond manual stock updates by introducing supplier records, purchase orders, and receiving workflows.
dependencies: Catalog and inventory foundations must remain stable first
Supplier purchasing should integrate with stock movement history rather than bypass it
exitCriteria: Suppliers become manageable first-class entities
Purchase order lifecycle is defined from draft to received
Stock receiving updates inventory through controlled domain rules

subIssues.title: [Suppliers][Next] Design supplier management module and shared contracts
deliverables: Define supplier entity, DTOs, and ownership boundaries
Design owner-facing supplier CRUD workflows and validation rules
Map how suppliers connect to products without duplicating catalog logic
acceptance: Supplier records have a clear backend source of truth
Frontend management flows consume shared contracts
Supplier-product relationships are explicit and maintainable

subIssues.title: [Procurement][Next] Implement purchase order draft, approval, and receiving flow
deliverables: Define purchase order states and line-item structure
Create owner workflows for drafting, confirming, and receiving orders
Route received quantities through inventory-safe stock updates
acceptance: Purchase orders have a controlled lifecycle
Receiving stock does not bypass inventory integrity rules
Order state and inventory impact are visible to operators

subIssues.title: [Suppliers+Procurement][Next] Plan operational reports for purchasing and stock intake
deliverables: Define the minimum reporting views for incoming stock and supplier activity
Identify reusable reporting contracts versus new procurement-specific metrics
Document the dashboard impact of supplier and receiving data
acceptance: Procurement reporting requirements are explicit before implementation
Metric ownership is clear between existing reports and new purchasing views
Future dashboard dependencies are known in advance

epics.title: [Next] Smart Inventory Automation and Forecasting
epics.summary: Add predictive restocking and barcode-assisted stock operations to move beyond manual stock supervision.
dependencies: Historical sales and inventory data must be reliable
Supplier and procurement structures improve the value of replenishment suggestions
exitCriteria: Restocking suggestions have a clear data basis
Barcode-assisted workflows reduce manual stock-entry friction
Operators can accept or reject automation recommendations explicitly

subIssues.title: [Forecasting][Next] Define replenishment suggestion engine inputs and outputs
deliverables: Specify the historical signals used for restock recommendations
Define suggestion payloads, confidence fields, and review states
Document what remains advisory versus fully automated
acceptance: Forecasting outputs are explainable to operators
Shared contracts define recommendation shape clearly
Automation boundaries are explicit and safe

subIssues.title: [Inventory][Next] Add barcode-assisted stock receiving and adjustment workflows
deliverables: Design barcode scan entry points for receiving and stock adjustment
Map scan results to existing product identity and stock movement logic
Define fallback behavior when product codes are missing or duplicated
acceptance: Barcode-assisted actions integrate with current inventory rules
Operator fallback paths are clear when scans fail
Scan-based workflows reduce manual product lookup friction

subIssues.title: [Forecasting+Inventory][Next] Prototype owner review UI for suggested replenishment
deliverables: Design a review queue for suggested restocks
Show the reasoning inputs that justify a recommendation
Define accept, dismiss, and defer actions for owners
acceptance: Owners can review recommendations without blind trust
Recommendation reasoning is visible enough to audit
UI actions map to intentional backend states

epics.title: [Later] Customer Retention and Multi-Store Expansion
epics.summary: Prepare the roadmap beyond MVP operations with loyalty mechanics, promotions, and scalable multi-store administration.
dependencies: Core single-store operations must be stable before cross-store complexity is introduced
Promotions and loyalty should build on trusted sales and product data
exitCriteria: The product has a clear path from store operations to growth features
Loyalty and promotion concepts are modeled without breaking POS clarity
Multi-store architecture assumptions are explicit before implementation

subIssues.title: [Loyalty][Later] Design customer, loyalty, and promotion domain boundaries
deliverables: Define customer identity, loyalty balance, and promotion eligibility concepts
Map how loyalty interacts with checkout without complicating cashier flows prematurely
Document the shared contracts needed for future implementation
acceptance: Loyalty concepts are modeled clearly before coding
Cashier experience remains a first-class constraint
Contract planning prevents ad hoc future types

subIssues.title: [Multi-Store][Later] Plan tenant, reporting, and administration expansion model
deliverables: Define what changes when one owner manages multiple shops
Review schema, authorization, reporting, and seed assumptions for multi-store scale
Identify which modules would require boundary changes first
acceptance: Multi-store impact is understood before schema changes begin
Authorization and reporting implications are explicit
A phased expansion strategy exists instead of speculative coding

subIssues.title: [Growth][Later] Define roadmap KPI model for retention and expansion features
deliverables: List the business KPIs needed for customer retention and store expansion decisions
Map which metrics can reuse the current reporting stack and which require new data structures
Document the implementation order that keeps analytics consistent
acceptance: Growth-oriented KPIs are scoped before implementation
Metric ownership is clear across current and future reporting
Expansion work has a measurable success model
